concepts.name: Cluster, nodes and control plane
concepts.summary: Explain that a cluster is made of worker nodes running workloads and a control plane (API server, etcd, scheduler, controllers) that manages desired state, with a kubelet on each node.

concepts.name: Pods as smallest unit
concepts.summary: Understand that a pod wraps one or more containers sharing network and storage, and is the unit Kubernetes schedules.

concepts.name: Declarative desired state
concepts.summary: Understand that you declare what you want and controllers continually work to make actual state match it.

concepts.name: YAML manifest structure
concepts.summary: Recognise and read the apiVersion, kind, metadata and spec fields of a Kubernetes manifest.

concepts.name: Basic kubectl commands
concepts.summary: Recall the commands to create, list, inspect and delete objects with kubectl (apply, get, describe, delete).

concepts.name: Labels and selectors
concepts.summary: Understand that labels are key-value tags on objects and selectors use them to group and target objects.

concepts.name: Namespaces for grouping
concepts.summary: Understand that namespaces partition resources within one cluster and that names are unique per namespace.

misconceptions.text: A pod is the same thing as a container and always holds exactly one container.
Kubernetes runs on the nodes only, and the control plane is just an optional dashboard.
Namespaces give strong security isolation between workloads by default.

concepts.name: ReplicaSets and replica counts
concepts.summary: Explain how a ReplicaSet keeps a specified number of matching pods running and replaces failed ones.

concepts.name: Deployments managing pods
concepts.summary: Write and apply a Deployment manifest and scale it, understanding it manages ReplicaSets that manage pods.

concepts.name: Services and ClusterIP
concepts.summary: Create a Service that selects pods by label to give a stable virtual IP and DNS name for reaching them.

concepts.name: Service types NodePort LoadBalancer
concepts.summary: Distinguish ClusterIP, NodePort and LoadBalancer Services and when each exposes a workload.

concepts.name: ConfigMaps for configuration
concepts.summary: Inject non-sensitive configuration into pods as environment variables or mounted files using ConfigMaps.

concepts.name: Secrets for sensitive data
concepts.summary: Create Secrets and consume them in pods via environment variables or volumes.

concepts.name: Logs and exec debugging
concepts.summary: Use kubectl logs, exec, describe and events to diagnose why a pod is failing or pending.

misconceptions.text: Secrets are encrypted, so base64 values in a Secret are safe from anyone who can read them.
You should create bare pods directly for production because Deployments add unnecessary overhead.
A Service's ClusterIP is reachable from outside the cluster.

concepts.name: Rolling update strategy
concepts.summary: Configure and perform rolling updates of a Deployment, tuning maxSurge and maxUnavailable.

concepts.name: Rollout history and rollback
concepts.summary: Monitor rollouts, inspect revision history and roll back a failed release.

concepts.name: Liveness readiness startup probes
concepts.summary: Analyse what each probe type does and choose probes so that restarts and traffic routing behave correctly.

concepts.name: Resource requests and limits
concepts.summary: Set requests and limits and analyse their effect on scheduling, throttling, OOM kills and QoS classes.

concepts.name: Ingress routing
concepts.summary: Define Ingress rules for host and path HTTP routing to Services, requiring an Ingress controller.

concepts.name: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler
concepts.summary: Configure an HPA to scale replicas on metrics such as CPU utilisation relative to requests.

concepts.name: Persistent volumes and claims
concepts.summary: Provide durable storage to pods using PersistentVolumeClaims and StorageClasses.

concepts.name: Helm charts and releases
concepts.summary: Install, upgrade and roll back Helm releases and override chart values.

misconceptions.text: A failing readiness probe restarts the container.
HPA scales on actual CPU usage alone, regardless of whether requests are set.
Creating an Ingress resource alone makes traffic flow, with no controller needed.

concepts.name: StatefulSet identity and storage
concepts.summary: Analyse how StatefulSets give pods stable names, ordered rollout and per-pod volumes, and when to choose them over Deployments.

concepts.name: Headless services for stateful apps
concepts.summary: Use headless Services to provide per-pod DNS records for peer discovery in stateful workloads.

concepts.name: Scheduling constraints and affinity
concepts.summary: Evaluate and apply selectors, affinity, taints and spread constraints to place pods for availability and isolation.

concepts.name: RBAC and service accounts
concepts.summary: Analyse and design least-privilege access with Roles, bindings and service accounts.

concepts.name: Network policies
concepts.summary: Restrict pod-to-pod traffic with NetworkPolicies, understanding they need a supporting network plugin.

concepts.name: Pod disruption budgets
concepts.summary: Evaluate how PodDisruptionBudgets protect availability during drains and upgrades.

concepts.name: Helm chart templating
concepts.summary: Author and review charts with templates, helpers and values that stay reusable and safe to upgrade.

concepts.name: Systematic troubleshooting workflow
concepts.summary: Diagnose failures such as CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, Pending and failing Services by tracing events, logs, selectors and endpoints.

misconceptions.text: A PodDisruptionBudget prevents involuntary failures such as node crashes.
NetworkPolicies work on any cluster regardless of the network plugin.
StatefulSets make a database highly available and consistent automatically.

concepts.name: Control plane internals
concepts.summary: Evaluate how API server, etcd, scheduler and controller manager interact and how their failure modes affect the cluster.

concepts.name: Custom resources and operators
concepts.summary: Design CustomResourceDefinitions and controllers that encode operational knowledge for an application.

concepts.name: Admission control and policy
concepts.summary: Evaluate admission controllers and policy engines to enforce security and governance rules.

concepts.name: Multi-tenancy and cluster design
concepts.summary: Design cluster and namespace topology balancing isolation, quotas, cost and blast radius.

concepts.name: Autoscaling at cluster level
concepts.summary: Evaluate how HPA, VPA and node autoscaling interact and design capacity strategies.

concepts.name: Progressive delivery and GitOps
concepts.summary: Design release pipelines using canary, blue-green and Git-driven reconciliation beyond basic rolling updates.

concepts.name: Upgrades and disaster recovery
concepts.summary: Plan and evaluate cluster upgrade, version skew and backup and restore strategies.

concepts.name: Observability and reliability engineering
concepts.summary: Design monitoring, alerting and capacity practices that make workloads and the platform reliable.

misconceptions.text: Running more replicas always guarantees high availability regardless of scheduling and dependencies.
HPA and VPA can safely scale the same pods on the same metric at the same time.
Operators are only needed for databases and replace the need to understand Kubernetes primitives.
